rules.description: Shortness of breath — high-risk chief complaint (odds ratio 43.7 for death or ICU in 72 h)
Altered mental status — high-risk chief complaint (odds ratio 6.2)
Vomiting blood — high-risk chief complaint (odds ratio 3.88)
Fall from height — high-risk chief complaint (odds ratio 3.88)
Weakness of one side of the body — high-risk chief complaint (odds ratio 3.16)
Chest pain — high-risk chief complaint (odds ratio 1.78)
Active seizures (fits reported — treated as active until a clinician confirms otherwise)
Systolic BP > 220 or diastolic BP > 110 mmHg
Systolic BP < 90 or diastolic BP < 60 mmHg
Active bleeding — nose, gums, vomiting blood or other
Altered sensorium — responds only to voice or pain, or unresponsive
Drowning, hanging, electrocution or trauma with a dangerous mechanism
Acute limb ischaemia — limb pulseless, or painful and pale/cold
Acute scrotal or inguinal pain in a male
Severe pain anywhere in the body (self-rated 7/10 or more)
Outside evaluation suggesting a time-sensitive emergency (ACS, dissection, stroke, sepsis, leukaemia, recent chemotherapy, potassium > 5.5)
Any two of — fever or hypothermia, headache, altered mental status, stiff neck
High-risk trauma — fall from height, road crash mechanism, penetrating, crush, injury in pregnancy, or injury on blood thinners / with a bleeding disorder
Major burn — face or neck, circumferential, inhalation injury, or more than 15 % of the body (both arms are 18 %)
Poisoning / ingestion or dangerous chemical exposure
Acute chest or abdominal pain, age over 50
Pregnant with heavy bleeding, severe abdominal pain, seizures or altered mental status, severe headache, visual changes, SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥110, active labour or trauma
Swelling or mass of mouth, throat or neck
New rash worsening over hours or peeling
Visible limb deformity, open fracture or suspected dislocation
Acute testicular / scrotal pain or priapism
Exposure requiring time-sensitive prophylaxis (animal bite, needlestick)
High-risk vital sign — heart rate < 60 or > 130
High-risk vital sign — respiratory rate < 10 or > 30
High-risk vital sign — AVPU other than Alert
Any two of — lethargy, sunken eyes, very slow skin pinch, drinks poorly
Altered mental status (confused, restless, irritable or lethargic) with stiff neck, hypothermia or fever
Age under 2 months with temperature < 36 °C or > 39 °C
High-risk trauma — fall from height, road crash mechanism, penetrating or crush injury, or injury on blood thinners / with a bleeding disorder
Major burn — face or neck, circumferential, inhalation injury, or more than 15 % of the body (both arms are 18 % in an adult, more in a child)
Acute testicular / scrotal pain or priapism
Poisoning / ingestion or dangerous chemical exposure
Swelling or mass of mouth, throat or neck
Any infant 8 days to 6 months old
Malnutrition with visible severe wasting or oedema of both feet
New rash worsening over hours or peeling
High-risk vital sign — AVPU other than Alert
High-risk respiratory rate for age under 1 — ≥ 50 or < 25
High-risk respiratory rate for age 1–4 — ≥ 40 or < 20
High-risk respiratory rate for age 5–12 — ≥ 30 or < 10
High-risk heart rate for age under 1 — ≥ 180 or < 90
High-risk heart rate for age 1–4 — ≥ 160 or < 80
High-risk heart rate for age 5–12 — ≥ 140 or < 70
General danger sign — unable to drink or breastfeed, vomits everything, convulsions, lethargic or unconscious
Stridor in a calm child (severe pneumonia or very severe disease)
Diarrhoea with two of — lethargic/unconscious, sunken eyes, not able to drink or drinking poorly, skin pinch very slow
Fever with stiff neck (very severe febrile disease)
Fast breathing — 60 or more per minute under 2 months
Fast breathing — 50 or more per minute at 2–12 months
Fast breathing — 40 or more per minute at 12 months to 5 years
Diarrhoea with two of — restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly/thirsty, skin pinch slow
Severe anaemia on report — Hb below 7.0 g/dL (pregnancy or child under 5)
Severe anaemia on report — Hb below 8.0 g/dL
Pregnant with BP ≥ 140/90 and urine protein 1+ or more on report (pre-eclampsia)
Coughing blood (screen for TB and other causes)
Chest pain spreading to arm, jaw or back, or with sweating (features of acute coronary syndrome) — whatever the onset
Severe hypertension (systolic ≥ 180 or diastolic ≥ 110 mmHg), or ≥ 160 / ≥ 100 with headache, visual change, chest pain, breathlessness or one-sided weakness — needs a doctor today
Presumptive TB (cough or fever for 2 weeks or more, or cough with weight loss or night sweats) — sputum test (NAAT) referral today
Late period or pregnancy with stomach pain, bleeding or fainting — pregnancy test and doctor today (rule out ectopic pregnancy)
Asthma or wheeze with SpO₂ below 94 % — not a mild flare; treat now and reassess within the hour

protocols.name: Pregnancy danger signs (WHO PCPNC, ISSHP, IITT)

rules.description: Severe hypertension in pregnancy — SBP ≥ 160 or DBP ≥ 110 mmHg
BP ≥ 140/90 with headache, visual disturbance or upper abdominal pain (possible pre-eclampsia)
Convulsions or altered consciousness in pregnancy
Fever and too weak to get out of bed
Fast or difficult breathing in pregnancy
Hypertension in pregnancy — BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg (needs review within 24 h)
Baby moving less than usual (same-day assessment)
Fluid leaking from the vagina (possible rupture of membranes)
New swelling of face or hands
Silica exposure with a presumptive TB symptom — same-day doctor review and NTEP sputum test (silicotuberculosis risk)
Dust exposure with cough or breathlessness for more than 8 weeks
Cough or breathlessness after 5 or more years of silica exposure
Breathing worse than at the last workplace screening
FEV1 down 15 % or more from the worker's own earliest recorded value

chest_pain_radiating: Chest pain spreading to arm, jaw or back
angioedema_face: Swelling of face, lips or tongue
swelling_mouth_neck: Swelling or mass of mouth, throat or neck
altered_mental_status: Confused, drowsy or not responding normally
one_sided_weakness: Weakness, numbness or drooping on one side; slurred speech
limb_weakness: Weakness of an arm or leg
skin_pinch_slow: Skin pinch goes back very slowly
scrotal_pain: Acute testicular / scrotal pain or priapism
rash_spreading: Rash worsening over hours or peeling
malnutrition: Visible severe wasting or swelling of both feet
burn_major: Burn of face, neck, both arms or legs, or most of the body
anticoagulated: On blood thinners or has a bleeding disorder
limb_deformity: Visible limb deformity, fracture or dislocation
threatened_limb: Limb pulseless, or painful with pale/weak/numb
tb_history: TB now or in the past
immunisation_incomplete: Vaccines not up to date for age
adherence_poor: Misses or has stopped regular medicines
known_time_sensitive_dx: Outside report of heart attack, stroke, sepsis, aortic dissection or leukaemia

threatened_limb: (arm|leg|hand|foot|limb) (is |has gone |turned )?(cold and pale|pale and cold|pulseless|blue and cold)
